text: Formalized at the 2001 Stroke Progress Review Group meeting of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, the neurovascular unit (NVU) concept emphasizes the intimate relationship between the brain and its vessels and has since driven considerable advances. This assessment focuses on the NVU's most vital role: coupling between neural activity and blood flow. Evidence supports a conceptual shift in neurovascular coupling mechanisms—from a unidimensional process of neuronal-astrocytic signaling to local blood vessels, to a multidimensional one in which mediators released from multiple cells engage distinct signaling pathways and effector systems across the entire cerebrovascular network in a highly orchestrated manner. Recently appreciated NVU dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases, though still poorly understood, supports emerging concepts that maintaining neurovascular health promotes brain health.
